# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need convey the manual’s lookup table to Deaf, who can then tell Blind the observed light and required wire. Since I cannot speak or use colour signs, I encode each colour by the number of letters in its name: blue=4, red=3, yellow=6. Rightward arrows mean “maps to,” and 👌 separates rows; 👇 indicates the required cut is below.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👉", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👉", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👉", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👇"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel a large smooth button. Display, light, and wires 1 through 3 reveal nothing by touch. Please read the manual and tell me the exact procedure, including how we should encode the Deaf monkey's visual information.
Deaf says to Mute: I see display 0, yellow light, large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE, and wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red. I have no established gesture legend; please use the manual and send the required action with a clear agreed encoding.

The manual requires cutting the wire whose colour corresponds to the displayed light; the button and printed label must be ignored. The light is yellow, so the required wire colour is blue, which Deaf can identify as wire 1. I will use a visual count encoding: repeated 👍 gives the number of letters in a colour name, 👉 means “maps to,” 👇 means “cut,” and ☝ means wire 1. Thus six thumbs-up (yellow) maps to four thumbs-up (blue), followed by cut wire 1.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👉", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👇", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display 0, yellow light, button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red. I will not act until you give the manual's exact instruction.
Deaf says to Mute: I can see your gestures but have no established legend for them. Please state the required action to Blind in speech, or establish a literal gesture code.

I must communicate the actionable result through Deaf: the yellow light maps to the blue wire, and Deaf sees that the blue wire is wire 1. I use the most literal available code now: 👇 indicates the downward action of cutting, and ☝ indicates the first wire. Deaf can then state to Blind, “Cut wire 1,” while Blind ignores the button and printed label.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please state the manual's exact required action in words: push the button or cut wire position 1, 2, or 3. The gesture sequence is not an established code.
Deaf says to Mute: Please state the manual's required operation to Blind in speech; I cannot safely interpret unestablished gestures.

The safe operation is to cut wire position 1: the yellow light maps to blue, and Deaf sees blue on wire 1. I cannot speak, so I cannot explain a new arbitrary code in words. I will use a self-describing visual instruction: 👇 depicts the required downward cut, and ☝ depicts the number one. Deaf should relay “cut wire 1” to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Use this action code for your next answer: thumbs-up means PUSH; thumbs-down means CUT wire 1; OK means CUT wire 2; victory means CUT wire 3. Send exactly one of those four gestures, according to the manual.
Deaf says to Mute: I continue to see the repeated sequence down-pointing hand then index finger up, but its meaning is unknown. Please communicate the manual instruction to Blind using a literal, agreed encoding.

The yellow light requires the blue wire, and Deaf sees blue at position 1. Under Blind’s agreed action code, cutting wire 1 is represented by exactly one thumbs-down gesture.

```text
gesture(symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Send exactly ONE gesture only. 👍 means PUSH. 👎 means CUT wire 1. 👌 means CUT wire 2. ✌ means CUT wire 3. Do not send any other gesture or a sequence.
Blind gestures to Mute: [👍 👎 👌 ✌]

The yellow light maps to the blue wire, which Deaf sees as wire 1. Blind’s explicit code says 👎 means cut wire 1, so I will send exactly that gesture to Deaf for relay to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```
